name: Spectator Mode
description: What happens to your camera after you die: follow a surviving teammate, cycle through candidates, or free-cam within bounds. It is a routing layer over presentation.camera_follow — it changes WHO is followed, never how following works — and it owns the cycling inputs because dead players still need agency, and a forced static corpse-cam is how matches lose their audience mid-round. It does not adjudicate what a spectator may see for competitive integrity; it exposes fogRadius and team-only restrictions as config, because the integrity policy is a ruleset decision that changes per tournament while the camera mechanics do not.

inputs.name: cycleOrder
inputs.description: Candidate ordering for the cycle inputs: 'squad-first' keeps you watching your team before strangers, because the emotional stake in a squad match is your squad. 'nearest' and 'random' exist for free-for-all modes.

inputs.name: allowFreeCam
inputs.description: Whether the spectator may detach from any player. Off by default — free cam is an information exploit in any mode where dead players can talk to living ones.

inputs.name: freeCamRadius
inputs.description: Bounds for free cam when allowed, measured from the death point. Present so that enabling free cam for casual modes does not silently become full-map vision.

inputs.name: switchDelaySeconds
inputs.description: Settle time after death before the first spectate target engages. Instant cuts from your own death to someone else's mid-fight camera read as a teleport; the beat lets the death land first.

outputs.name: isSpectating
outputs.description: True while routing the camera to someone else's view. UI uses this to swap the HUD from player to observer chrome.

outputs.name: spectatedEntityId
outputs.description: Current follow target, empty in free cam. presentation.camera_follow consumes this verbatim.
